name: Tourist Entry (CA-4)

requirements.blocker_text: Honduras is one of the four CA-4 Border Control Agreement countries (with El Salvador, Guatemala, Nicaragua); citizens of the other three CA-4 states enter on a national ID or passport alone. Non-exempt nationalities need either a Consular Visa (issued directly by a Honduran consulate, USD 30 single-entry/30 days or USD 60 multiple-entry/90 days) or a Consulted Visa (pre-validated by the National Immigration Institute -- INM -- before consular issuance, USD 100, required for certain nationalities and all legal entities). A visa does not guarantee admission -- the border officer makes the final call. Standard stay is 90 days, extendable once by 30 days at INM. As a CA-4 member, this 90-day allowance is shared across all four member countries and is not reset by crossing between them -- exiting to a non-CA-4 country is required to reset the clock.
requirements.fix_path: For non-visa-exempt nationalities, apply for a Consular or Consulted Visa through a Honduran consulate in advance.

evidence_required.document: Yellow fever vaccination certificate (if arriving from/departing to an endemic country)

outcome.duration_length: 90 days (shared CA-4 allowance), extendable once to 120 days

sources.title: Instituto Nacional de Migracion de Honduras -- visa categories (Consular, Consultada), CA-4 free-movement note, 90-day stay + 30-day extension

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Honduras). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- hard requirement sourced directly to inm.gob.hn (Honduras's own migration authority), tier 1. duration_type set 'rolling_window' consistent with how this dataset modeled Guatemala's CA-4 entry (gt_visitor_visa.json) -- Honduras is a CA-4 member on the same shared allowance, not a separate 90 days. The INM page did not itself publish a full visa-exempt nationality list (unlike, e.g., Zimbabwe's or Uzbekistan's e-visa portals) -- it names only the CA-4 partner states explicitly; other visa-exempt nationalities are referenced indirectly via the consular-fee schedule rather than listed by name, so a full country list is not asserted here.
